Hannibal.definition: Hannibal (Ann-) alis, *)anni/bas, a Carthaginian name: novus, i. e. an irreconcilable foe: ad portas (proverb. of imminent danger).

Harpyia.definition: Harpȳia (trisyl.), ae, f a Harpy: Celaeno, V. — Usu. plur., *(/arpuiai, the Harpies, rapacious monsters, half bird and half woman, V., H.

Heliades.definition: Hēliades um, f , *(hlia/des, daughters of Helios, changed into poplars, O.: nemus Heliadum, i. e. poplar-grove, O.; their tears became amber, hence, Heliadum lacrimae, i. e. amber, O.: capaces Heliadum crustae, i. e. …

Helvina.definition: Helvīna ae, f a surname of Ceres, Iu.

Hercules.definition: Herculēs is (rarely ī, C., Ta.), m a son of Jupiter and Alcmena, and god of strength, S., Cs., C., V., H., O.—As interj, by Hercules! assuredly, indeed: valde hercules vobis laborandum est.— With me: ego me hercules h…

Herculeus.definition: Herculeus adj. of Hercules, Herculean: manus, H.: coronae arbos, i. e. the poplar, V.: urbs, built by Hercules, O.

Hesperia.definition: Hesperia ae, f Hesperius; sc. terra, the land of the west, Italy , V., H.: ultima, i. e. Spain , H.

Hesperis.definition: Hesperis idis, f , *(esperi/s, of evening, of the west, western, V.—Plur. as subst, the daughters of Hesperus, guardians of the garden with golden apples, C., V., O., Iu.

Hesperius.definition: Hesperius adj., of Hesperus, of the west, western, H., O.: terra, i. e. Italy, V: Latium, V.

Hesperus.definition: Hesperus or -os ī, m , *(/esperos, the evening star, C., V., O.

Hilotae.definition: Hīlōtae (Ilō-) ārum, m , *ei)lw=tai, the bondsmen of the Spartans, Helots, N., L.

Hymen.definition: Hymēn (Hȳmēn, O.), —, *(umh/n, the god of marriage, god of weddings, Hymen (only nom sing.): Volgus ‘Hymen Hymenaee’ vocant, O., Ct.

Hymenaeus2.definition: Hymenaeus ī, m , *(ume/naios, the god of marriage, god of weddings, Hymen, Ct., O.

habena.definition: habēna ae, f HAB-, a holder, halter, rein : laeva, H.— Usu. plur: equorum per colla Excutit habenas, O.: omnīs effundit habenas, V.: effusissimis habenis, L.— A thong, strap : (turbo) actus habenā, V.: metuens pendent…

habens.definition: habēns adj. P. of habeo, owning, rich .—As subst m. : invidere habenti, V.

habeo.definition: habeō uī (old perf subj. habessit for habuerit, C.), itus, ēre HAB-, to have, hold, support, carry, wear : arma: anulum: arma hic paries habebit, H.: coronam in capite: soccos et pallium: catenas: Faenum in cornu, H.:…

habilis.definition: habilis e, adj. with comp. HAB-, easily handled, manageable, handy, suitable, fit, proper, apt, nimble, swift : arma: figura corporis: ensis, V.: arcus, V.: vigor, V.: brevitate gladii, L.: gens equis, expert , L.: it…

habilitas.definition: habilitās ātis, f habilis, aptitude, ability : habilitates corporis.

habitabilis.definition: habitābilis e, adj. habito, fit for an abode, habitable : regiones: cinguli (terrae): non habitabile frigus, O.

habitans.definition: (habitāns, ntis) m P. of habito, an inhabitant ; only plur gen. : habitantum, O.

habitatio.definition: habitātiō ōnis, f habito, a dwelling, habitation : ei de habitatione accommodare: sumptus habitationis: mercedes habitationum annuae, house-rent , Cs.

habitator.definition: habitātor ōris, m habito, a tenant, occupant, inhabitant : (domum) habitatores conduxerunt: tumultus habitatorum, L.: testā vidit in illā Magnum habitatorem, Iu.

habito.definition: habitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. habeo, to dwell, abide, reside, live : in aediculis habitat: in viā, on the high-road : in Siciliā: Lilybaei: lucis opacis, V.: sub terrā: ad Lepidum: apud te, T.: cum aliquo: alibi, L.: h…

habitudo.definition: habitūdō inis, f 1 habitus, condition, appearance : corporis! T.

habitus1.definition: habitus adj. with comp. P. of habeo, disposed, inclined : ut patrem tuom vidi esse habitum, T.— Well kept, fleshy, corpulent : (virgo) habitior, T.

habitus2.definition: habitus ūs, m HAB-, a condition, state, plight, habit, deportment, appearance, presence, mien : vir optimo habitu: corporis opimi: mediocris: oris et voltūs: habitūs corporum varii, Ta.: signa virginali habitu atque v…

hac.definition: hāc adv. abl f. of hic; sc. viā, this way, on this side, here : hac atque illac perfluo (i. e. passim), T.: Sequere hac me intus, T.: adire: Hac nostris erat receptus, Cs.: Hac iter est, V.: Hac fugerent Grai, Hac Phr…

hactenus.definition: hāc-tenus (hac . . . tenus, V., O.), adv., as far as this, to this place, so far, thus far: Hactenus crater erat asper acantho, O.: hactenus in occidentem Germaniam novimus, Ta.: Hac Troiana tenus fuerit Fortuna secut…

haedinus.definition: haedīnus adj. haedus, of a kid : pelliculae.

haedulus.definition: haedulus ī, m dim. haedus, a little kid , Iu.

haedus.definition: haedus (not hoedus), ī, m a young goat, kid, C., V., H., O.—Plur: Haedī, the Kids, two stars in the hand of the Wagoner (Auriga), C.: pluviales, V.—Sing: oriens, H.

haereo.definition: haereō haesī, haesūrus, ēre HAES-, to hang, stick, cleave, cling, adhere, hold fast, be fixed, sit fast, remain close : lingua haeret metu, T.: terra radicibus suis: scalarum gradū s male haerentes, holding : Haerent …

haeresis.definition: haeresis is, f , ai(/resis, a sect, school of thought: ea: Vestoriana, i. e. craft, trade.

haesitans.definition: haesitāns ntis, adj. P. of haesito, stammering : verba.

haesitantia.definition: haesitantia ae, f haesito, a stammering : linguae.

haesitatio.definition: haesitātiō ōnis, f haesito, a hesitating, stammering : quanta.—Fig.: mea, irresolution .

haesito.definition: haesitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. haereo, to stick fast, remain fixed : (eos) haesitantes premere, Cs.: in vadis, L.—Prov.: in eodem luto haesitare, i. e. to be exposed to the same danger , T.—Fig., to hesitate : linguā, …

hahae!.definition: 'hahae! or hahahae! interj, ha ha! T.'

haliaeetos.definition: haliaeetos (haly-) ī, m , a(liai/etos, an osprey, sea-eagle, O.

halitus.definition: hālitus ūs, m halo, breath, exhalation, steam, vapor : efflavit extremum halitum, his last breath : tenuis, breeze , V.: oris, Iu.

halo.definition: hālō āvī, ātus, āre AN-, to breathe, emit vapor, be fragrant : halantes floribus horti, V.: arae sertis halant, V.

hama.definition: hama (ama) ae, f , a)/mh, a water-bucket, fire bucket, Iu.

hamadryas.definition: hamādryas adis, f , a(madrua/s, a woodnymph, hamadryad, dryad, V., O., Pr.

hamatus.definition: hāmātus adj. hamus, furnished with a hook, hooked : ungues, O.: harundo, O.— Shaped like a hook, hooked, crooked : corpora: ensis, O.

hamus.definition: hāmus ī, m a hook: ferreae, Cs.: Lorica conserta hamis, of network, V.: pars pulmonis in hamis Eruta, the barbs (of an arrow), O.: hami curvi, talons, O.—A fish-hook, angle: Occultus, H.: praeroso hamo, after nibbling…

hara.definition: hara ae, f HER-, a pen, coop, sty : Claudor harā, O.: ex harā producte.

harena.definition: harēna (arēna) ae, f 2 HAS-, sand : harenam fluctū s trahunt, S.: bibula, V.: sterilis, V.: omnis Tagi, i. e. the gold , Iu.: nigra, slime , V.: carae harenae, golden sands , O.: urentes, H.— Prov.: Quid harenae semin…

harenaria.definition: harēnāria ae, f harena, a sand-pit .

harenosus.definition: harēnōsus (arēn-) adj. harena, full of sand, sandy : terra, O.: Litus, V.—As subst n., a sandy place , S.

hariolatio.definition: hariolātiō (ar-) ōnis, f hariolor, a soothsaying, prophesying , Enn. ap. C.

hariolor.definition: hariolor (ar-) ārī, ātus, dep. hariolus, to foretell, prophesy, divine : non hariolans, sed coniecturā prospiciens: quaestūs causā.— To speak foolishly, talk nonsense : hariolare, T.: hoc hariolor, am dreaming , T.

hariolus.definition: hariolus (ar-) ī, m HAR-, a soothsayer, prophet , T., C., Ph.

harmonia.definition: harmonia ae, f , a(rmoni/a, an agreement of sounds, consonance, concord, harmony.

harpago.definition: harpagō ōnis, m , a(rpa/gh, a hook, grappling-hook, grapple, drag, Cs., L.

harpe.definition: harpē ēs, f , a(/rph, a sickle-shaped sword, falchion, cimeter, O.

harundifer.definition: harundifer (ar-) fera, ferum, adj. harundo+ 1 FER-, reed-bearing, crowned with reeds : caput, O.

harundineus.definition: harundineus (ar-) adj. harundo, of reeds, reedy : silva, V.: carmen, a shepherd's song , O.

harundinosus.definition: harundinōsus (ar-) adj., abounding in reeds: Gnidos, Ct.

harundo.definition: harundō (arun-) inis, f a reed, cane: longa O.: fluvialis, V.: casae ex harundine textae, L.: harundinum radices, Cs.—A fishing-rod: captat harundine piscī s, O.: moderator harundinis, O.— Collect., limed twigs for ca…

haruspex.definition: haruspex (ar-) icis, m HAR-+4 SPEC-, a soothsayer, diviner, inspector of the entrails of victims : haruspices ex totā Etruriā: Tyrrhenae gentis, O.: ex prodigiis haruspices respondissent, S.: longaevus, V.— A prophet …

haruspicinus.definition: haruspicīnus (ar-) adj. haruspex, relating to soothsaying, of divination : libri.—As subst f . (sc. ars), divination .

haruspicium.definition: haruspicium (ar-) ī, n haruspex, inspection of victims, divination : Persicum, Ct.

hasta.definition: hasta ae, f 1 HAS-, a staff, rod, pole : gramineae, reeds of bamboo : foliis intexere hastas, the thyrsus , V.: foliis praesuta, O.: pura, i. e. without a head , V.— A spear, lance, pike, javelin : eminus hastis uti: …

hastatus.definition: hastātus adj. hasta, armed with a spear currūs, Cu.— Plur m . as subst, the hastati, spearmen, first line of a Roman army in order of battle , L.; consisting of ten ordines or companies, O.— Of the hastati, of the fir…

hastile.definition: hastīle is, n hasta, a spear-shaft, javelin-shaft : ferrum ex hastili, N.: hastili nixus: telum hastili abiegno, L.— A spear, javelin : Bina manu crispans hastilia, V.: Torquere hastilia lenta, O.: curvatum, Iu.— A pi…

hau1.definition: 'hau (au) interj. (of pain or grief), Oh! ah! T.'

haud.definition: haud or haut (hau, V.), adv., not, not at all, by no means : haud sane intellego, quid, etc.: res haud sane difficiles: haud ita iussi, T.: haud sic decet, T.: aliter, V.: diu, T.: minus, L.: sed haud facile dixerim, …

hauddum.definition: haud-dum adv., not at all as yet, not yet: cum patris favor hauddum exolevisset, L.: hiemps hauddum exacta, L.

haudquaquam.definition: haud-quāquam or haud quāquam by no means whatever, not at all: haud quaquam id est difficile Crasso: mediocre: par gloria, S.: certamine ambiguo, L.: dictis violentia Turni Flectitur, V.

haurio.definition: hauriō hausī, haustus (p. fut. hausūrus, V.), īre HAVS-, to draw up, draw out, draw : hausta aqua de puteo: palmis hausta duabus aqua, O.: aquam, H.: de dolio sibi hauriendum putet?— Prov.: tu quidem de faece hauris, …

haustus2.definition: haustus ūs, m HAVS-, a drawing : puteus facili diffunditur haustu, Iu.: aquae haustus, the right of drawing.—A drinking, swallowing, drawing in, drink, draught : exiguis haustibus bibi, in small draughts , O.: haustu …

haveo.definition: (haveō or aveō, —, —, ēre) imper. havē, havētō 1 AV-, to be well, fare well, be happy (only in salutation), S., Ct.

hebdomas.definition: hebdomas adis, f , e(bdoma/s, seven, the seventh day: quarta (critical in fever).

hebenus.definition: hebenus (ebe-) ī, f , e)/benos, the ebon tree, O.—Ebony: niger, V.

hebeo.definition: hebeō —, —, ēre hebes, to be blunt, be dull : ferrum nunc hebet? L.—Fig., to be sluggish, be inactive : Sanguis hebet, V.: sensu, O.: viri, Ta.

hebes.definition: hebes etis, adj. with comp, blunt, dull: tela hebetiora: ictus, O.: ferrum, Iu.—Dull, dim, faint: aures hebetiores: color, O.—Fig., dull, obtuse, sluggish, heavy, doltish, stupid<*> sensūs: homo: memoria: dolor: exerc…

hebesco.definition: hebēscō —, —, ere, inch. hebeo, to grow blunt, become dull, lose vigor, faint : mentis acies hebescit: hebescere sidera, Ta.: hebescere et languere nolumus: hebescere virtus, regard for character declined , S.

hebeto.definition: hebetō āvī, ātus, āre hebes, to make blunt, dull, blunt, dim, deaden, weaken : hastas, L.: ferrum hostium, L.: visūs tibi, V.: sidera, Ta.: taurorum flammas, quench the fiery breath , O.: alcui visūs, V.—Fig.: Lethe h…

hecatombe.definition: hecatombē ēs, f , e(kato/mbh, a sacrifice of a hundred oxen, hecatomb, Iu.

hedera.definition: hedera (ed-) ae, f HED-, ivy, ivy-vine (sacred to Bacchus, used in garlands): alba, V.: tabernacula protecta hederā, Cs.: doctarum hederae praemia frontium, H.: victrix, H.—Plur, ivyvines : nexiles, O., V.

hederiger.definition: hederiger (ed-) gera, gerum, adj. hedera+ GES-, ivy-bearing : Maenades, Ct.

hederosus.definition: hederōsus (ed-) adj. hedera, full of ivy : antrum, Pr.

hedychrum.definition: hēdychrum ī, n , h(du/xroun, a fragrant oiniment, cosmetic balsam.

hei.definition: hei interj. (of grief or fear), ah! woe! oh dear!: Hei mihi! V.

heia.definition: hēia (ēia) interj., of joy, ha! good! see! T. — Of eagerness, ha! see! quick! V., H.

helica.definition: helica ae, f , e(li/kh, a whorl.

helluatio.definition: helluātiō (hēlu-) ōnis, f helluor, a gormandizing, gluttony .

helluo.definition: helluō (hēluō) ōnis, m a gormandizer, glutton, squanderer, T.: patrimoni.

helluor.definition: helluor (hēluor) ātus, ārī, dep. helluo, to gormandize, devour : cum Graecis: meo periculo: tecum simul rei p. sanguine: parum, Ct.

helops.definition: helops (elops) opis, m , e(/lloy, the swordfish: pretiosus, O.

helvella.definition: helvella ae, f dim. helvus, yellow, a small potherb .

hem.definition: hem interj. (of surprise), oho! indeed! well! well, to be sure! hah!: hem, quid ais, scelus? T.: audistin? hem Scelera, T., C.

hemerodromus.definition: hēmerodromus ī, m , h(merodro/mos (all-day runner), a courier, L.—Plur: hemerodromoe, N.

hemicyclium.definition: hēmicyclium ī, n , h(miku/klion, a semicircle, semicircular recess, with seats.

hendecasyllabi.definition: hendecasyllabī ōrum, m , e(ndekasu/llaboi, verses of eleven syllables, Ct.

hepteris.definition: heptēris is, f , e(pth/rhs, a galley with seven banks of oars, L.

herba.definition: herba ae, f 1 FER-, an herb, grass, green blades, herbage, turf : in molli consedimus herbā, V.: abicere se in herbā: fusus per herbam, V.: corona ex asperis herbis: herbas omnīs condiunt: herbis Vivis et urticā, H.: …

herbescens.definition: herbēscēns ntis, adj. herba, appearing in green blades : viriditas.

herbidus.definition: herbidus adj. herba, full of grass, grassy : campus, L.: Epiros, O.

herbifer.definition: herbifer fera, ferum, adj. herba+1 FER-, producing grass, grassy : colles, O.: Acis, O.

herbigradus.definition: herbigradus adj. herba+GRAD-, going in the grass (of the snail), C. poët.

herbosus.definition: herbōsus adj. herba, abounding in grass, grassy : campus, H.: flumen, with grassy banks , V.: moretum, made with herbs , O.

herbula.definition: herbula ae, f dim. herba, a little herb .

hercisco.definition: hercīscō —, —, ere, inch. cf. herctum, to divide an inheritance : arbiter familiae herciscundae.

hercle.definition: hercle interj. contr. for hercule, by Hercules, assuredly, indeed : Puer herclest, T., C.

herctum.definition: herctum ī, n * hercio; cf. heres, an inheritance, patrimony : herctum ciere, to demand a partition .

hercule.definition: hercule interj. voc. of Hercules, by Hercules, assuredly, indeed : tum hercule confitear.—Often with me : vero me hercule hoc dicam.

here.definition: here adv. for herī, yesterday , C., H., O.

hereditarius.definition: hērēditārius adj. hereditas, of an inheritance, inherited, hereditary : ornamenta: cognomen: controversia.

hereditas.definition: hērēditās ātis (gen plur. -tātum, rarely -tātium), f heres, heirship, inheritance : nobilitas non hereditate relicta, S.: equum hereditate possidere.— An inheritance : hereditatem persequi, T.: hereditates mihi negast…

heredium.definition: hērēdium ī, n heres, an hereditary estate , N.

heres.definition: hērēs ēdis, m and f HER-, an heir, heiress : te ipso herede, T.: mulier facit heredem ex deunce Caecinam: in testamento heredes scripti, Cs.: testamento fecit heredem filiam: ex parte dimidiā: cur virgini Vestali sit …

heri.definition: herī adv. HES-, yesterday : quod mihi heri non licuit: heri vesperi; opp. hodie, O.— Lately, a short time ago , Ct., Pr.

heroicus.definition: hērōicus adj. , h(rwi+ko/s, of heroes, heroic, mythical: tempora: personae.

heroine.definition: hēroīnē ae, f (plur. īnae, Pr.), h(rwi/nh, a demi-goddess, heroine, Pr.

herois.definition: hērōis idis (dat plur. hērōisin, O.), f , h(rwi+/s, a demi-goddess, heroine, O.

heros.definition: hērōs ōis, acc. ōa, m , h(/rws, a demi-god, hero: heroum casūs: magnanimi heroes, V.: Aeneas, V.: Laertius heros, i. e. Ulysses, O.—A hero, illustrious man: noster Cato: cum heroibus nostris (i. e. Bruto et Cassio).

herous.definition: hērōus adj. , h(rw=os, of a hero, heroic: versus, epic: pes.

hesternus.definition: hesternus adj. HES-, of yesterday, yesterday's : dies: disputatio: ius, T.: convivium, L.: fercula, H.: Iacchus (i. e. vinum), drunk yesterday , V.: Lar, worshipped yesterday , V.

hetaericos.definition: hetaericos ē, on, f , e(tairiko/s, of comrades: equitum ala (in the Macedonian army), N.

heu!.definition: heu! interj., of grief or pain, oh! ah! alas!: heu nefas! H.: heu me miserum!: heu! miser, O.: Heu me! H.: Heu! heu! V.

heus!.definition: heus! interj., calling attention, ho! ho! there! lo! hark! holloa! Syre, Syre, inquam, heus, heus, Syre, T.: Heus, etiam mensas consumimus? V.: heus tu, Rufio.

hexameter.definition: hexameter trī, adj. , e(ca/metros, of six feet, hexameter: versus.

hexapylon.definition: hexapylon ī, n , e(ca/pulon, a gate of Syracuse with six passages, L.

hexeris.definition: hexēris is, f , e(ch/rhs, a galley with six banks of oars, L.

hiatus.definition: hiātus ūs, m hio, an opening, aperture, cleft : oris: terrenus, O.: atris inmanis hiatibus Hydra, open mouths , V.: personae pallentis, Iu.: repentini terrarum hiatūs: fontis, i. e. basin , O.: Quid dignum tanto hiatu…

hibernacula.definition: hībernācula ōrum, n dim. hiberna, tents for winter-quarters, an encampment for winter, winter tents : exercitu in hibernaculis conposito, S.: legionibus in hibernacula deductis, Cs.: hibernacula aedificari coepta, L.:…

hiberno.definition: hībernō āvī, ātūrus, āre hibernus, to pass the winter, winter, occupy winter-quarters : exercitum in agrum hibernatum duxit, L.: Pellae, L.: in sicco (naves), L.: quem ad modum milites hibernent: ubi sis hibernaturus.

hibernus.definition: hībernus adj. hiems, of winter, wintry, winter- : tempus anni: annus, i. e. winter-time , H.: ignis: grando, O.: soles, winter sunshine , O.: aequor, H.: pulvis, i. e. a dry winter , V.: vergens in occidentem hibernum…

hibiscum.definition: hibiscum ī, n , i)bi/skos, the marsh-mallow: gracilis, V.: viridis, V.

hic1.definition: hīc or hic f haec, n hōc or hoc (old, hōce, T.), gen. hūius (old, hūiusce, T., C.), plur. hī (hīsce, T.), f hae (old, haec, T., V.), n haec, gen. hōrum (hōrunc, T.—With the enclitic ne, usu. hicine; i. e. * hice-ne), …

hic2.definition: hīc (with the enclitic ne, written hīcine or hīcin), adv., in this place, here: ego hic adsum, T.: non modo hic, ubi . . . sed ubicumque, etc.: hic dux, hic exercitus; i. e. before us are, Ta.: Hic ubi Deucalion adhae…

hice.definition: (hice, haece, hoce) older form of hic, haec, hoc.

hiemalis.definition: hiemālis e, adj. hiems, of winter, wintry : hiemali tempore: vis: nimbi, O.

hiemo.definition: hiemō āvī, ātūrus, āre hiems, to winter, pass the winter, keep winter-quarters : quot annis: mediis in undis, H.: in Andibus, take up quarters for the winter , Cs.: legionem hiemandi causā conlocare, Cs.: scire ubi si…

hiems.definition: hiems (hiemps) emis, f cf. xeimw/n, the winter, winter time, rainy season : hieme summā, in the depth of winter : gravissimā hieme, Cs.: acris, H.: hiems appropinquabat, Cs.: hieme confectā, Cs.: Stridebat hiems, Iu.:…

hilare.definition: hilarē adv. with comp. hilarus, cheerfully, gayly, joyfully, merrily : sumamus diem, T.: res severas tractare: hilarius loqui.

hilaris.definition: hilaris e, adj. , i(laro/s, cheerful, of good cheer, lively, gay, blithe, merry, jocund, joyful: Oderunt hilarem tristes, H.: voltus: dies, Iu.: umbrae, Iu.

hilaritas.definition: hilaritās ātis, f hilaris, cheerfulness, gayety, joyousness, merriment, hilarity : hilaritatem illam amisi: hilaritatis plenum iudicium: in Laelio.

hilaro.definition: hilarō āvī, ātus, āre hilarus, to make cheerful, cheer, gladden, exhilarate : Periclis suavitate hilaratae Athenae: animum, Ct.: Hos ubi tua vox hilaraverit, O.

hilarulus.definition: hilarulus adj. dim. hilaris, cheerful, contented .

hilarus.definition: hilarus adj. with comp, cheerful, gay, merry, blithe, jocund, joyful: Hilarum fac te, cheer up, T.: convivae: voltus: Saturnalia: multo hilarior, T.: hilariores oculi.

hillae.definition: hillae ārum, f dim. hira; HAR-, a kind of sausage, smoked sausage , H.

hilum.definition: hīlum ī, n a shred, trifle (only with a negative): neque proficit hilum, a whit, Lucil. ap. C.

hinc.definition: hinc adv., from this place, hence: quae (via) est hinc in Indiam: hinc Romā venire: Illam hinc civem esse aiunt, T.—With iam, from this point onward, henceforth: maiora iam hinc bella dicentur, L.: iam hinc populi R. …
